nv_right_wall.blurb: A compact limestone sector on the right flank of the big Imagination Wall high in the Spring Mountains above Kyle Canyon, at roughly 8,000 feet. Nearly all of the 24 climbs are bolted sport lines, with a single trad route mixed in. The grades lean hard: a lone easy line and a few in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, then a thick cluster of 5.11s and 5.12s. Expect vertical faces on edges and runnels rather than big pockets. Being up at altitude, it is a place for cooler-weather escapes from the Las Vegas heat, and it suits strong sport climbers looking for sustained pitches more than beginners.

nv_left_wall.blurb: The left-hand section of the Imagination Wall on Mount Charleston, sitting near 8,100 feet in the Spring Mountains. It holds 24 climbs, all of them bolted sport routes on limestone, and most were added more recently than the neighbouring sectors. Difficulty centres on 5.10 through 5.12, with a pair of easier lines near 5.8 and one route reaching into the 5.13 range. The faces are vertical to slightly off vertical, with small edges and water-worn runnels for holds. A good pick for intermediate-to-strong sport climbers, with the elevation giving relief from valley temperatures in warm months.

nv_ginger_buttress.blurb: A triangular sandstone buttress on the east side of Rainbow Mountain at the mouth of Juniper Canyon in Red Rock, close to Las Vegas. Its full line is a long multi-pitch outing of well over a dozen pitches, while shorter routes on it make for moderate half-day objectives. Of the 24 climbs, almost all are trad, with a lone sport route and one aid line. Grades span 5.8 to 5.12, with the greatest concentration at 5.10 and 5.11. The climbing is mostly crack and face on chocolate-coloured rock, with a knife-edge arete high up. Wet sandstone breaks easily, so wait for dry conditions.

nv_north_face_2.blurb: The principal wall of Magic Mountain, a sandstone formation in Pine Creek Canyon in Red Rock. Its 23 listed routes are nearly all traditional, many of them multi-pitch lines of four to eight pitches up chimneys, pillars and varnished faces, plus a handful of shorter options. Grades run from about 5.7 up to 5.11, with most routes between 5.8 and 5.10. Because the wall looks north and sits across the creek, it stays in shade and tends to be cooler than the sunbaked walls nearby, which makes it a better bet in warmer months. Wet sandstone is fragile, so pick a dry spell.

nv_entrapment_wall.blurb: The biggest sector of the Upper Cliffs on the west side of Mount Potosi, southwest of Las Vegas, at about 5,600 feet. Its 23 bolted sport lines follow quirky features on limestone that was scorched by a wildfire before the bolting, so rock quality is variable though improving with traffic. Moderates are the strength: plenty of climbs from 5.7 to 5.10, a couple at 5.11, and a few harder lines up to the 5.13 range. Several of the best-liked routes earn around three stars. A good place for climbers working through the 5.8 to 5.10 grades who want an uncrowded, remote-feeling day on the hill.

nv_burglar_wall.blurb: A wall at the left edge of the main Robber's Roost cliff, off Deer Creek Road on Mount Charleston at close to 8,200 feet. All 23 climbs here are bolted limestone sport routes, and the grades skew very hard: a couple of 5.10s, then mostly 5.12 and 5.13 with a few in the 5.14 range. It faces north to west and stays shaded nearly all day apart from a little afternoon sun, which is why it is sought out when the Las Vegas valley is baking. Not a beginner venue, and the roadside pullout fills early on busy summer days.

nv_hamlet_the.blurb: A friendly sandstone crag in the Calico Basin part of Red Rock, reached on foot from the first parking pullout on the scenic loop. It has a two-tier layout, with most of the bolted sport routes on the upper level and a few top-rope lines below. Grades are easy to moderate, running from around 5.4 to 5.10, which makes it one of the better spots in the area for newer climbers and developing leaders. Over the years the rock has lost most of its loose holds. Like all Red Rock sandstone it is fragile when damp, so choose a dry day.

nv_east_face_3.blurb: The front side of Mescalito, the small formation just inside the mouth of Pine Creek Canyon in Red Rock. About 23 routes are listed, nearly all traditional, with a few top-rope lines, running from one to seven pitches. Difficulty starts near 5.7 and tops out in the 5.12 range, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10, so it suits confident trad climbers wanting moderate multi-pitch days. The sandstone is delicate when wet and can stay damp for days after a storm, so check conditions before heading up.
